reels.title: 5 St Andrew's Eve Love Spells
facts: St Andrew's Eve is the night of 29–30 November; in Poland it is called Andrzejki
Polish girls poured hot wax through the eye of a key into cold water and read their future from its shadow
Shoes were lined up from the wall to the door; the owner of the first to cross the threshold would marry first
In Romania, garlic was hung on doors and windows that night to keep away strigoi, the restless dead
Romanian girls slept with basil under their pillow to dream of their future husband
In German lands, girls prayed to St Andrew on Andreasnacht to see their future husband in a dream
reels.hook: Tomorrow night, summon your future husband

beats.text: 5 · Romania: garlic on every door against the dead
4 · Germany: pray to St Andrew, then dream of him
3 · Romania: basil under the pillow brings his face
2 · Poland: line up shoes; first out the door weds
1 · Poland: pour hot wax through a key, read its shadow

reels.caption:
Tomorrow night is St Andrew's Eve.

For centuries, girls across Eastern Europe used it to see who they would marry.

In Poland: hot wax poured through a key, its shadow read on the wall. Shoes walked to the door.
In Romania: basil under the pillow, garlic against the strigoi.

Would you try one tomorrow night?

reels.title: The Necromancy Rite Hidden in The Odyssey
facts: Book 11 of Homer's Odyssey, the Nekyia, describes Odysseus calling up the dead
The witch-goddess Circe gives him the instructions
He digs a pit about a cubit wide and pours milk and honey, then wine, then water, and sprinkles white barley
He sacrifices a ram and a black ewe, and the dead gather to drink the blood
The ghosts can speak to him only after drinking the blood
He holds the others back with his sword until the prophet Tiresias has drunk and foretold his journey home
reels.hook: Homer wrote a rite for raising the dead

beats.text: 5 · Book 11: Odysseus must question the dead
4 · The witch-goddess Circe teaches him the rite
3 · Dig a pit. Pour milk, honey, wine, water, barley
2 · Slay a ram and black ewe; the dead swarm
1 · Only after drinking blood can ghosts speak

reels.caption:
The Odyssey is in cinemas. Book 11 is the strangest part.

Circe tells Odysseus how to call up the dead: a pit, milk and honey, wine, water, barley, then the blood of a ram and a black ewe.

The ghosts crowd in. Only those who drink may speak. He holds them back with his sword until the prophet Tiresias comes.

Would you go down to the underworld for an answer?

reels.title: The Occult Roots of Queen Victoria's Mourning
facts: Prince Albert died on 14 December 1861
Queen Victoria wore mourning black from then until her death in 1901
Modern Spiritualism began in 1848 with the Fox sisters' rappings in Hydesville, New York
Séances became a fashionable entertainment in Victorian drawing rooms
The medium D. D. Home held séances for Napoleon III and Empress Eugénie
Stories that Victoria contacted Albert through a medium are legend, not documented

beats.text: 5 · Prince Albert died on December 14, 1861.
4 · Victoria wore black until her death in 1901.
3 · Séances became the fashion in Victorian drawing rooms.
2 · D. D. Home held séances for Napoleon III.
1 · Did Victoria contact Albert? Legend, not record.

reels.caption:
Victoria wore black for 40 years.

Albert died in December 1861. She mourned until her own death in 1901, and her age became obsessed with the dead.

Séances filled Victorian drawing rooms. Mediums performed for emperors.
And the story that Victoria reached Albert through a medium? Legend, not record.

Have you ever attended a séance?

reels.title: Krampus Comes Tomorrow Night
facts: Krampus is a horned, hairy demon of Alpine folklore who travels with St Nicholas
Krampusnacht is 5 December, the eve of St Nicholas' Day
St Nicholas rewards good children while Krampus punishes bad ones
He carries birch switches and rattling chains, and sometimes a basket to carry children off
In Krampus runs, men in carved wooden masks and sheepskins parade through Alpine towns
Krampus greeting cards, 'Gruß vom Krampus', were popular from the late 1800s

beats.text: 5 · A horned Alpine demon who walks with St Nicholas
4 · Nicholas rewards the good. Krampus punishes the bad
3 · Birch switches, chains, a basket for children
2 · Masked men in sheepskins still run through Alpine towns
1 · 5 December: Krampusnacht. Lock the door

reels.caption:
Tomorrow is Krampusnacht.

On the eve of St Nicholas' Day, the saint brings gifts to good children. His companion comes for the rest: horned, hairy, carrying birch switches, chains and a basket.

In Alpine towns, masked Krampus runs still fill the streets.

Were you told about the Krampus as a child?
